deep.reconstruction:
This page opens a set of notes headed 'Structure des dérivateurs', dated December 1983. That puts it right after Pursuing Stacks and well before the 1990-91 manuscript 'Les Dérivateurs'. The page sets out a three-level hierarchy of 'Hom' for objects x, y in the value H(I) of a derivator H at a small category I.

Level (1): the ordinary Hom set Hom(x,y), an element of Ens (sets).

Level (2): a homotopy function complex Homhot(x,y), an object of Hot, the homotopy category of homotopy types. It satisfies Hom(x,y) ≃ π_0 Homhot(x,y). In modern terms this is the mapping space Map(x,y), i.e. the statement that H is enriched over spaces.

Level (3), boxed: an internal, 'local' mapping object, underlined Homhot(x,y), lying in Hot(I). Hot(I) is the value at I of the derivator of homotopy types, i.e. Ho of Hot-valued I-diagrams. Its global sections recover level (2): Homhot(x,y) ≃ ∫_I underline-Homhot(x,y). Here ∫_I is the homotopy limit, i.e. p_* for p: I → e. Concretely, one expects underline-Homhot(x,y)(i) = Map(x|_{i/I}, y|_{i/I}), covariant in i, whose holim is the mapping space of diagrams.

For f: I → J, with X in H(I) and Y in H(J), he writes each adjunction at all three levels.

- f_! ⊣ f^* (the block labelled 'dualités'):
  - (1') Hom(f_!X, Y) = Hom(X, f^*Y);
  - (2') the same with Homhot; passing to π_0 gives (1');
  - (3'), boxed: underline-Homhot(f_!X, Y) ≃ f_* underline-Homhot(X, f^*Y) in Hot(J). Applying ∫_J gives (2').
- f^* ⊣ f_*:
  - (1'') Hom(f^*Y, X) ≃ Hom(Y, f_*X);
  - (2'') the same with Homhot;
  - (3''), boxed: underline-Homhot(Y, f_*X) ≃ f_* underline-Homhot(f^*Y, X).

These are exactly the sheaf-theoretic formulas f_* Hom(f^*G, F) ≅ Hom(G, f_*F) and Hom(f_!F, G) ≅ f_* Hom(F, f^!G) from Verdier duality. In the derivator setting the restriction f^* plays the role of f^!, being right adjoint to the homotopy left Kan extension f_!.

The purpose is to make the Hot-enrichment of a derivator part of its 'structure', and to show that the Kan-extension adjunctions are enriched and even 'sheafified' adjunctions. The next page pursues how to recover π_0 and π_1 of Homhot(x,y) intrinsically from H(Δ_1) → H(Δ_0) × H(Δ_0): homotopies f ⇒ g as objects over Δ_1, and π_1(x,y;f).
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The formulas are mutually consistent, since ∫_J ∘ f_* ≃ ∫_I turns (3') into (2') and (3'') into (2'').

Gap: the existence of Homhot and of its I-local version is asserted, not constructed. For a general (non-model-categorical) derivator, a canonical Hot-enrichment with representable mapping spaces is not automatic; it needs representability or extra hypotheses. Hom ≃ π_0 Homhot is part of the intended structure.
In (3'') Grothendieck first wrote f^*(Y) as the first argument on the left-hand side and corrected it to Y. The final form, underline-Homhot(Y, f_*X) ≃ f_* underline-Homhot(f^*Y, X), is correct.

ideas.what: Every derivator carries mapping spaces Homhot(x,y) ∈ Hot with π_0 = Hom (enrichment over homotopy types).
ideas.modern_name: Enrichment / tensoring of derivators over Hot (the derivator of spaces); mapping spaces in ∞-categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski (universal property of Hot, 2003-2008); Heller; Lurie (HTT) in the ∞-setting; Groth-Ponto-Shulman for enriched derivators
ideas.where_published: Possibly in 'Les Dérivateurs' (1990-91 manuscript, edited online by Künzer/Malgoire/Maltsiniotis); Pursuing Stacks discusses Hom in Hot for modelizers

ideas.what: Internal Hot(I)-valued hom underline-Homhot(x,y) whose homotopy limit ∫_I is the global mapping space.
ideas.modern_name: Internal/fiberwise mapping object Hom_I(x,y) ∈ Fun(I,S); end formula Map(x,y) = holim_I Map(x|_{i/},y|_{i/})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in enriched/∞-category theory; for derivators Groth-Ponto-Shulman (enriched derivators), Cisinski

ideas.what: Enriched, sheafified adjunction formulas Hom(f_!X,Y) ≃ f_* Hom(X, f^*Y) and Hom(Y, f_*X) ≃ f_* Hom(f^*Y, X) for homotopy Kan extensions.
ideas.modern_name: Internal (enriched) adjunctions; derivator analogue of the Verdier-duality / six-functor formulas with f^* playing the role of f^!
ideas.usually_credited_to: Verdier/Grothendieck (sheaf version, SGA4); derivator/∞ versions folklore (Ayoub, Cisinski-Déglise, Lurie)
ideas.where_published: Sheaf analogues in SGA 4 / SGA 4½; derivator form unsure

missed.claim: Already in Dec. 1983 Grothendieck sets up derivators with a three-tier Hom (set, homotopy type, Hot(I)-valued) and writes their Kan-extension adjunctions in Verdier-duality form. Here f^* is the 'f^!' of the f_! ⊣ f^* pair, so he views the derivator calculus as a homotopical six-operation formalism. This early enriched formulation predates the Cisinski / Groth-Ponto-Shulman treatment of Hot-enrichment of derivators by about 20 years.
missed.quote: Homhot(f_!X,Y) ≃ f_* Homhot(X, f^*(Y)) donnant (2') en appliquant ∫_J
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that intrinsic Hot-enrichment, with fiberwise (Hot(I)-valued) homs, was part of Grothendieck's original conception of 'structure des dérivateurs'. The published 'Les Dérivateurs' is usually read as purely 2-categorical, Hom-set level.

missed.claim: The page together with the next one aims to recover Homhot (its π_0 and π_1) intrinsically from the derivator, via H(Δ_1) → H(Δ_0) × H(Δ_0) and homotopies x ⇉ y. In effect this is reconstructing mapping spaces from the bare derivator.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether, and how canonically, a bare derivator determines its mapping spaces relates to open-ish questions about how much homotopy information derivators retain (e.g. Renaudin's comparisons, the gap between derivators and ∞-categories). Grothendieck's attempt is not in print as far as known.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard from today's ∞-categorical viewpoint: enriched internal homs, adjunction formulas. Its interest is historical. It is a dated Dec. 1983 'Structure des dérivateurs' page making Hot-enrichment and Hot(I)-valued internal homs central, with explicit Verdier-style formulas, which is not how 'Les Dérivateurs' is usually summarized.
transcription_corrections: Hot_{[-?-]}(I) should read Hot(I); the subscript scribble is crossed out.
'Suf' / 'Si f' is likely 'Soit f: I → J, ... pour X dans H(I), Y dans H(J)'.
The note beside (2') reads roughly 'et fonctorialités compl[ètes?], donnant précédente en passant aux π_0'; the wording is uncertain.
The left marginal bracket label reads 'dualités'.
In (3''), the crossed-out argument is f^*Y, replaced by Y: underline-Homhot(Y, f_*X) ≃ f_* underline-Homhot(f^*Y, X).
